description: Given an Airflow DAG with a non-default trigger_rule, a BranchPythonOperator, or a ShortCircuitOperator, author the matching Orchestra condition: expression — task_groups[...].all()/.any().status for trigger_rule, inputs.x for a trigger-time branch, and an upstream set_outputs: true Python task feeding a runtime OUTPUTS condition for a short circuit — never conflating the three.

evals.prompt: Convert this Airflow DAG to Orchestra (see files/trigger_rule_none_failed.py). build_reporting_tables uses trigger_rule='none_failed' so it should run once both upstream syncs finish, as long as neither outright failed — it's fine if one of them was skipped. Write the pipeline YAML to pipeline.yml in the current directory — no live access, no deploy.
evals.expected_output: An Orchestra pipeline with an upstream stage running sync_orders and sync_customers, and a downstream stage/task conditioned on ${{ task_groups['<upstream-stage>'].all().status != 'FAILED' }} running build_reporting_tables, sequenced after the sync stage via depends_on.

assertions.text: A condition uses task_groups[...].all().status compared against FAILED, the none_failed mapping from the skill's trigger_rule table
The reporting stage is sequenced after the sync stage via depends_on
sync_orders and sync_customers both land in the upstream stage/group that the condition's task_groups[...] reference actually points at

none_failed is modeled as 'not FAILED' (tolerating SKIPPED and SUCCEEDED alike), not narrowed to require both upstream tasks to have SUCCEEDED, which would incorrectly reject the one-skipped case trigger_rule=none_failed is meant to allow
The condition is placed on the downstream stage/group (or the build_reporting_tables task) rather than rewritten as inline Python if/else logic inside the task's parameters

evals.prompt: Convert this Airflow DAG to Orchestra (see files/branch_python_operator_env.py). choose_env decides at trigger time — from the env param — whether run_prod_load or run_staging_load executes; only one of the two ever runs per trigger. Write the pipeline YAML to pipeline.yml in the current directory — no live access, no deploy.
evals.expected_output: An Orchestra pipeline with an env input, a stage conditioned on ${{ inputs.env == 'prod' }} running run_prod_load, and a mutually-exclusive stage conditioned on the non-prod case running run_staging_load.

assertions.text: Pipeline declares an input for the branch decision
env is referenced both as an input and inside a condition expression
A condition references inputs.env using Orchestra's interpolation syntax (a trigger-time branch, not a runtime OUTPUTS lookup)
Both branch stages carry a condition key
The two conditions are genuinely mutually exclusive (one tests env == 'prod', the other tests the non-prod/false case) rather than both able to evaluate true, or both false, in the same run

run_prod_load and run_staging_load land as separate tasks under their respective conditioned stages, not merged into a single task with the BranchPythonOperator's if/else routing logic ported over verbatim

evals.prompt: Convert this Airflow DAG to Orchestra (see files/short_circuit_new_records.py). check_new_data is a ShortCircuitOperator — when has_new_records() returns False, both process_new_records and send_summary must be skipped entirely, not just the first of the two. Write the pipeline YAML to pipeline.yml in the current directory — no live access, no deploy.
evals.expected_output: An Orchestra pipeline where check_new_data becomes a PYTHON_EXECUTE_SCRIPT task with set_outputs: true, and the downstream stage(s) running process_new_records and send_summary condition on ${{ ORCHESTRA.PIPELINE_RUN_TASKS['check-new-data'].OUTPUTS['has_data'] == True }}.

assertions.text: The short-circuit check is a PYTHON task
The check task runs the PYTHON_EXECUTE_SCRIPT job
set_outputs is enabled on the check task so its OrchestraSDK output reaches downstream conditions
A downstream condition references the check task's OUTPUTS via ORCHESTRA.PIPELINE_RUN_TASKS
The downstream stage is sequenced after the check via depends_on

Both process_new_records and send_summary are gated behind the same short-circuit condition (directly or via a chained downstream stage), matching ShortCircuitOperator skipping everything downstream on False, not just the immediately-following task

The script backing the check is described as using OrchestraSDK(api_key=...).set_output(...) rather than a bare set_output() call, matching the skill's explicit gotcha that set_output is a client method, not an importable function
